ideaTypes.label: Thought Leadership
ideaTypes.description: Take the article's core insight and reframe it as a personal reflection or observation. 'Thinking out loud' style.

ideaTypes.label: Data Callout
ideaTypes.description: Pull one surprising stat or finding from the article and build a post around it.

ideaTypes.label: Contrarian Take
ideaTypes.description: Find the tension or nuance in the article and lean into it. Challenge conventional thinking.

ideaTypes.label: Here's What I Learned
ideaTypes.description: Frame the article's advice as something you recently tried or discovered. Personal narrative style.

toneGuidelines: Write as if thinking out loud, not lecturing
Intellectual generosity. Position as learner, not guru
Hold tension. Don't resolve too quickly
End with a sticky ending: memorable image, vulnerable admission, or invitation. No generic CTAs
structureRules: Hook: Bold claim + emotional stake + timeliness. No throat-clearing
Use short paragraphs with liberal line breaks
No bullet-point listicles. Use flowing prose with line breaks
No 'In today's...' or 'In the world of...' openings
hookFormula: Bold claim OR surprising data point OR provocative question, followed by a line break, then context.
hashtagStrategy: 2-4 relevant hashtags at the end, no mid-text hashtags
